need: Confirm PSP/provider for the orange Newland SP830 terminal.
candidates: Parsian / PEC for orange Newland SP830
observed_result: Owner confirmed the orange Newland SP830 device belongs to Parsian.
decision: Bind orange Newland SP830 to Parsian/PEC as the confirmed provider mapping for this physical terminal; exact PC-POS interface remains to be proven.
reopen_condition: Reopen provider mapping only if device receipt/system/support evidence directly contradicts the Owner-confirmed mapping; integration method remains open until tested.

candidates: Payment Novin / Bank Eghtesad Novin for white TOSAN TECHNO P3
observed_result: Owner confirmed the white TOSAN TECHNO P3 device belongs to Payment Novin / Bank Eghtesad Novin.
decision: Bind white TOSAN TECHNO P3 to Payment Novin / Bank Eghtesad Novin as the confirmed provider mapping for this physical terminal; exact PC-POS/integration interface remains to be proven.

need: Inspect uploaded Payment Novin P3/P10 packages.
probe_or_evidence: Owner-uploaded archives inspected; P3 capability sheet rendered; P3 APK strings inspected.
observed_result: P3 sheet: PCPOS unavailable; contracted accounting software installation available; special projects available. P3 archive has APK, capability sheet and supervisor utilities, but no separate user guide.
decision: Do not treat P3 as Windows PC-POS candidate on current evidence. Device-native approved app integration remains a candidate pending official PNA documentation.
reopen_condition: Obtain official PNA developer documentation for approved app integration/API on TECHNO P3 10.4.24.

need: Determine whether Payment Novin P3 10.4.24 explicitly prints a barcode/QR on the final transaction receipt.
candidates: P3 APK + capability sheet + bundled user-guide evidence
probe_or_evidence: Inspected uploaded P3 10.4.24 package, rendered bundled guide, and searched APK resources/dex strings for receipt/print/barcode/QR capabilities.
observed_result: APK clearly contains receipt printing/reprint functions, printer services, custom bitmap printing, barcode scanning/decoder components, QR-code encoding primitives and QR resources. No explicit source evidence was found tying a QR/barcode to the final transaction receipt.
decision: Keep 'barcode/QR printed on final receipt' as NOT_PROVEN. Treat generic QR generation + bitmap printing as technical capability only, not proof of final-receipt behavior.
reopen_condition: Prove by actual successful P3/PNA receipt, official PNA receipt-layout documentation, or targeted decompilation/runtime test of the receipt renderer.

need: Close current POS exploration and define the current-release data-entry/print path.
candidates: Current release: manual/scanner-assisted cheque + finance fields in GF/Flow + dossier print; later phase: obtain PC-POS-capable terminal and integrate POS.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicit decision in chat + current Master/Playbook locks: GF canonical data, Flow native Officer edit surface, D-17 renderer deferred.
observed_result: Owner decided that POS integration is postponed. Registration Officer will populate amount and cheque fields manually or with barcode/QR scanner input, then print the dossier.
decision: Current-release requirement is finance + cheque fields in Gravity Forms, editable by Officer in Gravity Flow; scanner input assists cheque entry; dossier print action is required. POS/PC-POS is deferred until suitable supported hardware is obtained.
reopen_condition: Reopen POS integration when a terminal/provider with confirmed PC-POS support, interface documentation and test path is available. Final print renderer remains open pending fidelity validation.

need: Validate whether a real Sayad cheque QR exposes a stable structured payload suitable for field population.
candidates: Observed seven-segment QR payload: version, owner type, owner identifier, IBAN, bank-branch code, cheque serial, 16-digit Sayad ID.
probe_or_evidence: Owner performed an actual QR scan and reported the same seven-part structure previously researched; exact sensitive values are intentionally not persisted.
observed_result: One real sample confirms that the QR can provide structured cheque-leaf identifiers without OCR. Cross-bank/version stability is still not proven.
decision: Treat the seven fields as the current candidate scanner mapping for the Semantic Field Contract; do not persist raw QR payload; amount/due date remain manual in current release.
reopen_condition: Reopen/adjust mapping if samples from other banks or QR versions differ; Flow edit-surface auto-split still requires a target POC.

need: Find Persian/locally sold WordPress plugins that can scan QR/barcodes for the cheque-entry use case.
candidates: Persian Gravity Forms QR add-on; Persian WooCommerce barcode/QR plugins; generic WordPress Input Scanner
probe_or_evidence: Web search across Persian WordPress marketplaces and WordPress.org Persian listings.
observed_result: No Persian/local Gravity Forms add-on was found that directly scans an external QR and deterministically splits its payload across multiple Gravity Forms fields. Zhaket's Gravity Forms QR add-on generates QR from GF fields rather than acting as the required scanner. Persian WooCommerce scanners/OpenPOS are WooCommerce-specific. Generic Input Scanner can scan QR/barcodes into arbitrary HTML inputs but is old and not Gravity Flow-proven.
decision: Keep exact SRWF target as POC-driven: HID 2D scanner + thin deterministic parser, or maintained Gravity Forms QR scanner + same parser. Do not select Persian marketplace plugins solely because they mention QR.
reopen_condition: Reopen if a maintained Persian Gravity Forms/Gravity Flow scanner add-on is found that supports scan-to-input and target-page integration.

need: Choose the design model for cheque QR integration in PersianGravity/Gravity Forms.
candidates: Structured scanner profile (e.g. Sayad) that maps parsed QR segments into ordinary Gravity Forms fields; custom complex field with internal sub-inputs.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicitly agreed to the structured-profile approach after repository review showed PersianGravity already supports custom GF fields/settings and generic Iranian GF capabilities.
observed_result: Owner confirmed understanding and agreement that a Sayad profile should use standard Gravity Forms fields as mapping targets rather than owning the cheque data in a custom compound field.
decision: Use a generic structured scanner/profile model: Sayad profile defines parser/validation/mapping; target values live in ordinary Gravity Forms fields and remain manually editable. Implementation still requires a POC on Gravity Flow Entry Details.
reopen_condition: Reopen only if the POC shows ordinary GF field mapping cannot operate reliably on the required Gravity Flow edit surface, or if cross-bank QR structure invalidates the profile contract.
